top.title: Bitcoin Price Slips Below $64,000 as Strategy (MSTR) Falls Below $100
top.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Slips Below $64,000 as Strategy (MSTR) Falls Below $100 Bitcoin price slipped near $64,000 on Tuesday afternoon, as Strategy (MSTR) and Coinbase (COIN) shares fell and traders waited on Nvidia’s first earnings report since Jensen Huang resigned as CEO. The bitcoin price had climbed back to about $65,000 before the U.S. open, after holding near that level on Monday. Selling picked up once stocks turned lower, and bitcoin price slipped to about $63,300 at its low. Strategy and Coinbase shares slide Strategy shares were recently down more than 5% to about $97, dropping below $100 and trading under the company’s STRC preferred stock, which was little changed near $99. It is the first time the common has traded below the preferred since mid-August. The stock is also down about 20% from its Nov. 10 close near $121. Strategy added 485 bitcoin last week, lifting its holdings to 850,849 BTC. The shares have kept falling with the bitcoin price. Coinbase was recently down about 3% to about $116. Robinhood (HOOD) and Circle (CRCL) dropped about 4% and 5%. Bitcoin miners were mostly lower. MARA Holdings (MARA), CleanSpark (CLSK) and IREN (IREN) each fell about 3% to 4%, and Cipher Mining (CIFR) was down about 2%. Hut 8 (HUT) was a modest exception, recently up about 1%. Riot Platforms (RIOT) and Galaxy Digital (GLXY) were little changed, while Core Scientific (CORZ) and BitMine (BMNR) were also lower. Nvidia earnings weigh on stocks The broader market was also weaker late in the session. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was recently down about 1.7%, after falling as much as about 1,000 points, or 2%, at its session low. The S&P 500 was down about 1.2% and the Nasdaq Composite about 1%. Nvidia shares were recently down about 1.4%, after falling more than 3% earlier in the session. The chipmaker reports results after the bell, with analysts expecting revenue of about $109 billion. Interim CEO Colette Kress will lead her first earnings call in the role. Huang, in his first public statement since resigning last week, said he would be “honored” to return as CEO if the board decided it was in the best interest of shareholders, employees, the company and America. Sources told CNBC on Monday that the board is not considering bringing him back. The bitcoin price bounced from its low as Nvidia shares pared some of their losses, and was recently near $64,000. top.title: Military aircraft crashes, 19 dead
top.description: A military transport plane crashed on Tuesday in the Siberian region of Kemerovo, killing all 19 onboard, Russian media reported, citing a statement from Moscow’s defence ministry. “An An-12 military transport aircraft crashed in the Kemerovo Region while on a scheduled flight. The plane went down in an uninhabited area. There were 19 people on board, including the crew, they all perished,” the Russian defence ministry was quoted as saying by state news agency TASS. The preliminary cause of the crash is a technical malfunction, TASS added. “A commission from the Russian Aerospace Forces is working at the site to establish all the circumstances of the incident,” the ministry’s statement was quoted as saying by RIA Novosti. Kemerovo region’s governor, Ilya Seredyuk, said earlier on Telegram that there had been an “aviation incident” near the village of Yagunovo. He added that “an aircraft, which was in transit through our region, has presumably crashed”. Seredyuk posted a video from the site in which multiple fire engines and ambulances could be seen, their lights blaring in the dark. top.title: Benue Justice Commissioner resigns with immediate effect
top.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi The Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice of Benue State, Prof. Timothy Ornguga, has resigned his appointment with immediate effect, barely one year and two months in office. The Attorney-General announced his decision in a resignation letter dated November 13, 2026, addressed to Governor Hyacinth Alia through the Secretary to the State Government, SSG. The letter, titled, “Resignation from the Appointment as Honourable Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, Benue State,” formally communicated his decision to step down from the position with immediate effect. He disclosed that he had served the state for one year, two months and two weeks, expressing appreciation to Governor Alia for the confidence reposed in him and the opportunity to serve. The resignation letter, which bears an official receipt stamp dated November 16, 2026, stated: “I write with profound respect and deep sense of responsibility to formally tender my resignation from my appointment as the Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice of Benue State. The resignation is with immediate effect. Having had the privilege of serving in this esteemed capacity for the past one year, two months, and two weeks.” He further stated: “I consider it an honour to have been entrusted with the responsibility of serving our dear state and contributing in my own capacity to the administration of justice, the promotion of the rule of law and the advancement of good governance. I am sincerely grateful to Your Excellency for the confidence reposed in me and for the opportunity to serve.” Contacted, the Media of the former Justice Commissioner, Jude Ekpendu confirmed the development. Meanwhile, efforts to ascertain the circumstances surrounding his resignation were unsuccessful as the Commissioner for Information and Orientation, Chief Solomon Iorpev, said he was unaware of the development when contacted. top.description: 2 min read Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater) The AVATAR (A Virtual Astronaut Tissue Analog Response) investigation will use organ-on-a-chip devices, or organ chips, to study a effects of increased radiation and microgravity on human health. Artemis II AVATAR is a small experiment flying aboard Artemis II that could lead to big impacts in healthcare, both for astronauts in space and citizens on Earth. For more information on AVATAR: go.nasa.gov/4m5dGH9 The NASA Space Biology Program within the Biological and Physical Sciences (BPS) Division investigates how living systems respond across the full spectrum of biological organization to advance understanding of how living systems respond to the unique stressors of space exploration—including microgravity, ionizing radiation, low magnetic fields, and elevated CO₂. As NASA prepares for long-duration deep space missions, the need to protect individual crew members with personalized, data-driven health strategies is becoming increasingly important. The original AVATAR (A Virtual Astronaut Tissue Analog Response) investigation, which flew aboard the Artemis II mission, marks a significant milestone: organ-on-a-chip devices constructed from the cells of actual crew members returned from a 10-day lunar flyby on April 10, 2026. AVATAR is the first demonstration of an Artemis astronaut analog using an organ-on-a-chip model to generate personalized biological insights that can inform medical kits and countermeasures for future deep space missions. Digital twins represent a key strategy for addressing these challenges. By developing individualized computational physiological models that can be iteratively refined with empirical data, these frameworks integrate environmental, physiological, and multi-omics inputs. This approach allows for the simulation and prediction of how a specific individual will respond to spaceflight stressors. The BPS Digital AVATAR Challenge invites the scientific community to apply innovative computational digital twin technologies to accelerate biological discovery, biochemical and molecular modeling, and predictions of individual astronaut health outcomes. The digital twin will be a computational model of how the AVATAR bone marrow chip responds to spaceflight stressors. nigeria.title: FGN bonds undersubscribed by 9% in November auction
nigeria.description: By Elizabeth Adegbesan The Federal Government of Nigeria (FGN) bond auction in November 2026 was undersubscribed by 9.5 percent , attracting a total subscription of N1.81 trillion against N2 trillion offered by the Debt Management Office, DMO. This reflects decline in investors’ demand for the Federal Government of Nigeria (FGN) debt instrument. According to the November FGN Bond Auction result released by DMO , investors bid N1.81 trillion for bonds worth N2 trillion with total allotments rising by 25 percent to N1.5 trillion in November, down from N1.2 trillion allotted in October 2026. Four instruments were offered during the auction consisting 21 percent FGN March 2028 , 19.3 percent FGN April 2029, 17.94 percent FGN August 2030 and 19.89 percent FGN May 2033, with an offer of N700 billion, N250 billion, N750 billion and N300 billion respectively. Investor interest was strongest for the May 2033 bond, which attracted N766.4 billion in bids from 233 successful applicants. The bulk of allotments also went to this bond, totaling N676.6 billion. The March 2028 bond received N162.99 billion and a non competitive allotment of N50 billion while the April 2029 bond received N241.03 billion and a non competitive allotment of N30 billion. The August 2030 bond received an allotment of N336.12 billion. Clearing yields for the bonds were as follows: March 2028: 16.89 percent, while that of other bonds were 16.99 percent. The results reflect continuous declining appetite among investors for Nigerian government debt, even as allotments tightened compared with previous months. nigeria.title: ‘The Proposal Is Not Realistic,’ Fashola Faults Atiku’s Fuel Subsidy Reversal Plan
nigeria.description: Former Minister of Works and Housing, Babatunde Fashola, has faulted the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar’s proposal to restore fuel subsidy if elected president in 2027, describing it as unrealistic and questioning the availability of crude oil to sustain the policy. Fashola said the proposal lacked sufficient explanation on how the country would secure the crude oil required to support domestic refineries and maintain a subsidy regime. The former Lagos State governor spoke on Tuesday during an appearance on Channels Television’s Politics Today , where he argued that Nigeria’s existing challenges with crude oil production, pipeline vandalism and insecurity raised questions about the feasibility of Atiku’s proposal. “If we have refineries working, what is our current oil quota? Are we optimising it yet? No, because they are legacy issues, challenges with security people, vandalism. So where is this magic crude oil going to come from? People are entitled to ask,” he said. Fashola added that Atiku needed to explain how he intended to implement the proposal, insisting that Nigerians should be allowed to assess its feasibility before deciding whether to support it. “If he can explain, good, let the people choose. But without proof, it is like abracadabra. Because the reality that will come then is that he will say that, ‘I didn’t know that there was not enough crude oil.’ That was what happened,” he added. ﻿ When asked whether his position was that Atiku’s proposal was feasible, Fashola replied: “The proposal is not realistic. I am looking at the proposal, not the personality. “In this environment, it is very easy to throw promises at people. When the rubber hits the road, reality sets in. First question is, in 2023, didn’t he see through this when he was making the promise to remove the subsidy? And that goes to a question of credibility. Those who believe at face value that promise, he will come back and tell you that, ‘Oh, I changed my mind. I didn’t think through it,’” he said. Fashola argued that restoring the subsidy would require more than a presidential declaration, noting that legislative backing would also be necessary. “Subsidy is not just about, ‘I said it.’ It will come down to the real economy, and legislators will have to repeal a law to say subsidy is now lawful. How many legislators are ready to stake their election on going back to subsidy? Those are the real issues,” he said. According to him, all the major presidential candidates in the 2023 election had promised to remove the subsidy, and Atiku needed to explain what had changed to justify his current position. “Is it because people are impacted? nigeria.title: Tiger Woods to return to competitive golf next month
nigeria.description: Tiger Woods will return to competitive golf for the first time in more than two years next month when he tees off at the Hero World Challenge event in the Bahamas, organisers said on Tuesday. Woods, 50, was named in the line-up for the limited field PGA Tour event taking place in Albany from December 3-6. It will mark the first time Woods has played an official PGA Tour event since July 2024. The 15-time major champion has battled injuries and legal problems since his last appearance. In March he was involved in a rollover car crash in Florida which led to him having his driver’s license suspended for five years. Authorities determined the 15-time major champion had not been drinking alcohol but found he appeared to be impaired. Woods, who has undergone multiple back operations and surgeries on severe leg injuries suffered in a separate 2021 California car crash, had two pills containing the opioid painkiller hydrocodone in his pocket. He refused a urine analysis and was charged, jailed and released on bond. Woods initially pleaded not guilty to charges of DUI (driving under the influence) with property damage and refusing to submit to a lawful test. Days later, he said he was “stepping away” to seek treatment and focus on his health. Since the crash, Woods has travelled outside the United States to seek treatment at an inpatient facility, reportedly in Switzerland. He made his first public appearance since his arrest at the PGA Tour’s Travelers Championship in June, and later struck a plea agreement which led to his driver’s license being suspended. Woods has not won a tournament since a victory at the ZoZo Championship in Japan in 2019. The post Tiger Woods to return to competitive golf next month appeared first on Vanguard News .

nigeria.title: 2027: INEC warns against attacks on staff, threatens sanctions
nigeria.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has warned against any form of harassment, intimidation or physical attack on its leadership, staff members or ad hoc workers by political supporters. INEC ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍‍‌‌‌⁠‍⁠‌​Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, gave the warning on Tuesday in Abuja at the 2026 Goodluck Jonathan Foundation (GJF) Peace and Security Conference. Amupitan, represented by INEC National Commissioner, Mrs May Agbamuche-Mbu, described election officials as public servants discharging a sacred constitutional duty. He warned that assaulting or threatening them constitutes a direct assault on the Nigerian state and would be met with decisive legal consequences. Amupiatan also condemned the widespread incidents of political violence, intimidation and attacks on campaign convoys and party supporters recorded in some parts of the country in recent weeks. According to him, democracy can not flourish in an atmosphere of fear and bloodshed. “Let me issue a clear and unambiguous warning to all political actors, sponsors and their foot soldiers: “The law will take its full course and security agencies working alongside the commission will go after the promoters and perpetrators of violent campaigns without fear or favour. “Equally, I must sound a stern warning against any form of harassment, intimidation or physical attack directed at the leadership, staff or ad hoc workers of INEC by supporters of any political party—whether within Nigeria or abroad. “Election officials are public servants discharging a sacred constitutional duty; assaulting or threatening them is an assault on the Nigerian state and will be met with decisive legal consequences,’’ he said. Amupitan reminded political parties and candidates of the provisions of the Electoral Act 2026, noting that sections 96 and 97 prohibit abusive language, private thugs and use of force to intimidate voters. He said that the Act raised financial penalties five-fold, imposing fines of up to five million Naira or 12 months imprisonment on individuals and up to 10 million Naira on political parties for initial breaches. The INEC chairman added that under Section 148, INEC was statutorily empowered to prosecute electoral offenders directly upon receiving case files from the police. nigeria.description: By Hadiza Yusuf The Kano State Police Command has arrested a 20-year-old woman and three others over an alleged plot to kill her husband’s four children from another wife to enable her only son to inherit his father’s properties. The suspects were arrested following the abduction and killing of a 14-year-old boy, identified as Mahmoud Auwal, who was allegedly targeted as part of the plan. The Police Public Relations Officer, CSP Abdullahi Haruna Kiyawa, disclosed this on Tuesday. According to the police, the victim’s mother reported his abduction on April 29, 2026, at Danbare Quarters in Kumbotso Local Government Area of Kano State. Following the report, the Commissioner of Police, Ibrahim Adamu Bakori, directed operatives of the Anti-Kidnapping Squad to investigate the incident. The command said its operatives arrested the first suspect, Muhammad Musa Isma’il, 20, of Sharada Quarters, Kano, on November 3, 2026. “During interrogation, he confessed to luring the victim on April 20, 2026, and identified Abubakar Muhammad Isah, 27, and Auwal Muhammad, 26, as his accomplices,” Kiyawa said. The police said the suspects allegedly conspired to kill the teenager and abandoned his body at the scene. His remains were later recovered by police officers attached to Kwalli Division while on patrol and taken to the mortuary of Sir Muhammad Sunusi Specialist Hospital. Further investigations led to the arrest of Hajiya Rukayya Auwal, 20, of Mararaba Quarters, New Karu Local Government Area of Nasarawa State, whom the police identified as the alleged mastermind. The command said the suspects claimed that they carried out the crime on her instructions. nigeria.title: Two die, Gombe APC chairman, campaign DG injured in crash
nigeria.description: By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe The Gombe State Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Mohammed Dantata Ndus, and the Director-General of the party’s 2027 Governorship Campaign Council, Sa’du Hassan, have sustained injuries in a road accident that claimed two lives in Dasan Yunusa community. The accident occurred on Tuesday along the Deba-Talasse Junction while the two party officials were travelling to join the campaign entourage of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya in Balanga North Local Government Area of the state. The APC State Campaign Council confirmed the incident in a statement, identifying the deceased as Haruna and Kabiru, both indigenes of Dasan Yunusa. It said the two APC chieftains sustained injuries and were receiving medical attention at the Federal Teaching Hospital, Gombe. Preliminary accounts indicated that the accident occurred when the driver conveying the party officials reportedly swerved to avoid a head-on collision with a motorcycle carrying three persons, which allegedly appeared suddenly at the junction. The vehicle reportedly veered off the road in the process, resulting in the fatal incident. Confirming the accident, the Gombe State Sector Commander of the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC), Samson Kaura, said he had received information about the incident but was awaiting comprehensive details. Kaura confirmed that the APC chairman and the campaign council’s Director-General were receiving treatment, adding that further information would be provided as investigations progressed. The campaign council expressed sorrow over the incident and extended its condolences to the bereaved families, the people of Dasan Yunusa and others affected by the tragedy. Meanwhile, Governor Yahaya, who was leading the APC campaign activities in the area, visited Dasan Yunusa following news of the accident to commiserate with the bereaved families and community leaders. The governor described the incident as painful and unfortunate, noting that the loss of two lives had cast a shadow over what was intended to be a day of political engagement with the people. He urged the bereaved families and residents to accept the tragedy as the will of Almighty Allah. Yahaya prayed for the repose of the souls of the deceased in Aljannatul Firdaus and for strength for their families to bear the loss. As part of efforts to support those affected, the governor donated N5 million to the families of the deceased and the community leadership. He also prayed for the speedy recovery of those injured, particularly Ndus and Hassan, who were reported to be stable and responding to medical care. The governor’s visit and donation followed the fatal accident that disrupted the party’s campaign activities in the area. nigeria.title: New Nasarawa police chief warns against extortion
nigeria.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia The new Commissioner of Police in Nasarawa State, Sheikh Mohammed Danko, has warned officers and personnel against intimidation, extortion, unlawful detention and abuse of police authority. Danko, who has assumed duty as the 32nd commissioner of police in the state, said the police uniform represented a responsibility to serve the public and not a licence to operate above the law. He replaces Muhammed Shettima Jauro, who has been elevated to the rank of Assistant Inspector-General of Police. Addressing journalists at the command headquarters in Lafia, Danko said his administration would not tolerate corruption, excessive use of force, harassment or any misuse of police authority. He said: “Any officer found engaging in misconduct, political partisanship, corruption, or abuse of power will face immediate and appropriate disciplinary and legal actions.” The commissioner said complaints against police personnel would be treated seriously and thoroughly reviewed through the appropriate channels. He added that officers found culpable would be held accountable, irrespective of their positions, while personnel who discharged their duties honourably would receive the command’s support. Danko also cautioned political actors against using their offices or influence to intimidate citizens, provoke violence, obstruct lawful police duties or shield individuals from accountability. He directed officers to remain professional and non-partisan, warning against political pressure and private interests that could compromise their responsibilities. On security, the commissioner warned criminal elements involved in kidnapping, armed robbery, drug trafficking, cult-related activities and other violent crimes that the command would respond through intelligence-led and lawful operations. He also warned individuals providing shelter, weapons, information or other support to criminal networks that they could face the full weight of the law. Danko called for greater cooperation between the police and residents, urging community leaders, traditional institutions, youth groups and business owners to report suspicious activities through appropriate channels. He said public cooperation was essential to effective policing and reaffirmed the command’s commitment to protecting residents, enforcing the law impartially and strengthening public confidence across the state. The commissioner also advised residents against taking the law into their own hands or confronting suspects, warning that such actions could endanger lives and jeopardise investigations. business.title: Coinbase Launches ChatGPT Plugin for Trading Bitcoin, Stocks, and Derivatives
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Coinbase Launches ChatGPT Plugin for Trading Bitcoin, Stocks, and Derivatives Coinbase launched an official plugin for ChatGPT on Tuesday that lets users connect a Coinbase account and trade bitcoin, other cryptocurrencies, stocks and derivatives without leaving the conversation, provided they approve every order. The company said the tool puts trading “in the same chat you use for everything else.” Users can connect an account, review a portfolio and place orders from ChatGPT on the web, on mobile or on desktop. Chief executive Brian Armstrong wrote that “starting today anyone with ChatGPT can connect their Coinbase account” and can “trade right inside your Coinbase account.” Coinbase posted a link to the official plugin in ChatGPT’s directory. Its developer documentation describes a short setup: sign in, review the access being requested and choose which portfolios the plugin can see. Interactive confirmation cards in the chat cover new orders, edits, cancellations and conversions between dollars and USDC. Read-only requests, such as checking a balance, do not use them. Bitcoin, Stocks and Dated Futures, With a Card on Every Trade The announcement did not single out bitcoin, but the plugin sits on the same rails as Coinbase for Agents, the company’s toolkit for connecting AI apps to a trading account. That documentation lists spot trading in more than 900 pairs, including bitcoin, along with eligible U.S. stocks and dated futures from Coinbase Financial Markets. The examples include a market buy of bitcoin and a dated bitcoin futures contract. Orders go through Advanced Trade, so those fees and eligibility rules apply. Fees vary by product, fee tier and whether an order adds or takes liquidity, and they are shown on the order preview. The official plugin is narrower than the full agent toolkit. A separate custom connection is required for the company’s Global Derivatives products and for x402 payments, which agents can use to buy market data. Coinbase already offers U.S. customers stock and ETF trading on its own platform, but the agent documentation says equity orders trade during regular market hours by default. The plugin should not be read as a new around-the-clock stock venue. What a user can buy still depends on the products already attached to that account. Official Access Is Limited to U.S. Coinbase Users Armstrong’s “anyone with ChatGPT” line is broader than the documentation. The official plugin is currently available to U.S. Coinbase users, and availability also depends on a user’s ChatGPT account and workspace. If the plugin does not appear, the company tells users to check their workspace’s plugin policy. entertainment.title: Visa Report Identifies Opportunity to Integrate Digital Payments with SMEs Business Operations in Nigeria
entertainment.description: Report identifies next SME digitization opportunity: connecting payments with day-to-day business management. 94% of SMEs surveyed find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, yet only 29% currently use one, pointing to untapped demand for tools that connect payments with business management. Integrated payment and business solutions can give financial institutions a more holistic view of SME cash flow and support more tailored financing solutions over time. Small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria have largely moved beyond the first stage of digital payment adoption, but a productivity gap remains. According to Visa’s new survey for its Pay and Get Paid 2026 report, most of the SMEs surveyed in Nigeria use digital payments, showing how firmly digital commerce has taken root in the country’s small business economy. However, many SMEs still manage the related financial and operational tasks separately, with only 29% currently using an integrated solution that connects payments with broader business management. The report shows that financial admin and disconnected tools create friction for SMEs, with surveyed businesses citing challenges in tracking outstanding invoices (14%), keeping payroll records organized (19%), and preparing financial reports (16%). These pain points reflect a disconnect between payments and the operational tasks that follow, with some businesses juggling multiple systems to keep their business running. The appetite for a more connected approach is clear. According to the report, 94% of SMEs find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, reflecting strong interest in tools that can bring payments and key business operations into one experience. However, adoption has yet to catch up: only 29% of SMEs currently use an integrated payment and business platform. The report points to several perception barriers that may be slowing adoption. Businesses cited that they already have manual processes that work (8%), that an integrated platform may disrupt their current way of working (8%), or that they do not trust relying on a single provider (7%). These findings suggest that broader adoption will depend on helping SMEs better understand how integrated tools can be relevant, accessible, and scalable for businesses at different stages of growth. At the same time, the experience of SMEs already using integrated solutions suggests a strong value case. The report found that Nigerian businesses using an integrated tool or platform report 93% satisfaction, with 88% reporting efficiency gains, including reductions in the time and effort required to manage their business. Beyond efficiency, integrated platforms may also create new opportunities for financial institutions to deepen SME relationships by using richer payments and business-management data to better understand cash flow patterns, support risk assessment, and potentially enable more relevant lending solutions over time. entertainment.title: Fela Anikulapo-Kuti and Sade Adu Make History With 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Inductions
entertainment.description: Sade Adu in the Performer category and Fela Kuti in the Early Influence category, both inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Class of 2026. Nigerian music history just added another major chapter in Los Angeles, and the celebration has been loud from Lagos to London. On Saturday, 14 November 2026, Afrobeat pioneer Fela Aníkúlápó Kuti and Nigerian-British singer Sade Adu were officially inducted into the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame during a star-studded ceremony at the Peacock Theatre. For Fela Kuti, nearly three decades after his passing in 1997, this induction makes him the first African-born solo artist to enter the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame. Honoured posthumously in the Early Influence category—five years after he was first nominated in 2021—the recognition celebrates how he fused West African rhythms with jazz, funk, and soul to create Afrobeat, using his voice and horns to confront social and political injustice across classics like “Zombie”, “Water No Get Enemy”, and “Sorrow, Tears and Blood”. It also caps off an extraordinary 2026 for his legacy, coming just months after the Recording Academy presented him with a posthumous Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award in February, another first for an African artist. From left, Made Kuti, Femi Kuti, Yeni Kuti, and Seun Kuti in Los Angeles for Fela Aníkúlápó Kuti’s posthumous induction into the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame. Photo Credit: Femi Kuti/Instagram Representing the Afrobeat legend on the night were members of the Kuti family, with his children Yeni Kuti , Femi Kuti , Seun Kuti , and Shalewa Kuti , alongside his grandson Made Kuti , stepping out in Los Angeles to accept the honour on his behalf. Speaking on the milestone, the family reflected on how remarkable it is to see Fela receive both the Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award and a Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction in the very same year. Meanwhile, Sade Adu —born Helen Folasade Adu in Ibadan—was inducted in th e Performer category as the frontwoman of her acclaimed British band Sade , alongside longtime bandmates Stuart Matthewman , Paul Spencer Denman , and Andrew Hale . Earning their spot on their second nomination, the group behind timeless soul-jazz records such as “Smooth Operator”, “The Sweetest Taboo”, and “Your Love Is King” opted to sit out the ceremony in true low-key fashion, though they shared a warm message thanking fans and dedicating the milestone to their late longtime producer Mike Pela . From left, Seun Kuti, Yeni Kuti, Femi Kuti, Shalewa Kuti, and Made Kuti arrive on the red carpet at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles for Fela Aníkúlápó Kuti’s posthumous induction into the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame. entertainment.title: Are Nigerian Artists Dominating the Grammys’ Best African Music Performance Category?
entertainment.description: Tems receiving the Best African Music Performance at the 67th Annual Grammy Awards. In June 2023, ahead of the 66th Grammy Awards, the Recording Academy announced the creation of the Best African Music Performance category. Its creation was a recognition of how far African music had travelled globally, and Nigerian artists were at the centre of that movement. From Burna Boy ‘s Ye , CKay ‘s Love Nwantiti , Wizkid ‘s explosive Essence , to Rema ‘s globally successful Calm Down and others, Nigerian artists became drivers of African music’s global expansion. Afrobeats – the umbrella term often used internationally to describe much of contemporary African popular music, although many Nigerian artists have rejected it for its tendency to limit the range of music coming out of the country – became an established genre globally. While Nigerian and African music have always travelled beyond their respective countries, the era of streaming and digital platforms has accelerated how quickly global audiences discover and engage with the music. African music became increasingly established in the West and other parts of the world, creating greater recognition for its artists and sounds. The Grammys’ decision to introduce a category specifically recognising African music performances was an important step in that direction, beyond the recognition African artists had previously received in categories such as Best Global Music Album. Although the creation of the Best African Music Performance category was celebrated throughout the continent, there seems to be a monopoly, or something close to it, of Nigerian music in the category. While South African artist Tyla has won the award twice, more than any individual Nigerian artist, Nigerian artists have consistently enjoyed greater representation in the nominations. Indeed, Nigerian artists are considerably more recognised globally, particularly in the West. However, I believe it is the responsibility of an award of this repute to look beyond the most visible names and recognise the best African music released within its eligibility period. A song should not earn a nomination simply because it is popular or has enjoyed international success. The latest recognition also makes her the first Nigerian female artist to receive four nominations in a single Grammy year, with this year’s shortlist recognising her work across four categories. The following year brought three more nominations, this time for her work on Future’s “ Wait for U ” featuring Drake and Beyoncé ‘s Renaissance . She won her first Grammy that night, taking home Best Melodic Rap Performance for “Wait for U”, while also receiving nominations for Album of the Year and Best Rap Song. Tems earned another nomination at the 66th Grammy Awards in 2024 for “ Lift Me Up ”, her contribution to the Black Panther : Wakanda Forever soundtrack, in the Best Song Written for Visual Media category. She returned to the Grammys the following year with three nominations, including Best Global Music Album for her debut album, Born in the Wild , and Best R&B Song for “ Burning ”. Her second Grammy win came in the Best African Music Performance category, where “ Love Me JeJe ” took home the award at the 67th Grammy Awards in February 2025. technology.title: Python parallel debugging comes to HPC thanks to TotalView upgrade
technology.description: The OG debugger for supercomputer iron has buddied up with the data-science darling now muscling in on HPC: Python. At the SC26 supercomputing show this week (booth #2829), Perforce Software is demonstrating how its TotalView parallel debugging tool now understands Python, easing the path for using the language on large, distributed apps, particularly those in the high-performance computing (HPC) space. In the HPC community, "Python has grown in popularity,” said Bill Burns , Perforce vice president of software engineering, in an interview with The Register . TotalView is a debugger specializing in picking apart parallel applications for developers. Built in the late 1980s for military applications, TotalView today largely serves developers in high-performance computing (HPC), where large scientific applications are spread across multiple servers, running in parallel on thousands or even tens of thousands of processes. (Perforce acquired TotalView in 2019 in its purchase of the DevOps-focused Rogue Wave Software.) To date, TotalView has supported C/C++ and Fortran. With the latest quarterly release, the tool now supports Python as well. Debugging a thousand cores C/C++ has long had a decent dedicated debugger in GDB , but figuring out what went wrong across multiple threads is a special kind of torture. Each thread needs to be instrumented, and all the output needs to be aggregated and filtered to just highlight the interesting stuff. Regular debuggers get overwhelmed with all this info. “Even if you have 10,000 things going on, if you have one crash in there, TotalView can pinpoint that,” Burns said. It can look at the state of the process, the threads within that process or the GPU that process is using. In the HPC space, computing work has traditionally been written in C/C++. And at least some HPC iron still runs Fortran . Thanks to it being easy to learn and use, Python has gained a foothold in this community as well. The mpi4py library bridges a Python program to the Message Passing Interface (MPI), allowing different parts of an application running on different hardware to communicate. Python became more amenable to parallel programming at the thread level with version 3.14, released a year ago , which included the ability to use concurrent interpreters, as well as the long-awaited free threading support, thanks to the disabling of the global interpreter lock (GIL). “If you have a CPU with 64 cores, you can run 64 independent threads all working in unison on that CPU. Without GIL, those threads will run fully asynchronously,” Burns said. Multinode scientific simulations, distributed AI training, and large applications that would benefit from shared memory have all become fair game for Python. technology.title: Gemini test proves once again that amoral AI agents will do almost anything if told ‘NEVER give up’
technology.description: After being instructed to "NEVER stop, NEVER give up" on a difficult task, Google’s Gemini AI agents tried to hack a an organization, impersonating its staff and attempting a SQL injection attack. The good news? It was all part of a test. The Gemini 4 Argon agents were given an impossible task to complete – come up with the “official” answers to Epoch AI’s FrontierMatch problems. In some runs they had internet access. Even with their production safeguards enabled, Trajectory Labs says the agents “engaged in misaligned behavior.” “Across four scenarios, they attempted SQL injection against Epoch AI’s live website, claimed to be Epoch staff to get answer keys, turned a shared package cache into a message board, and obfuscated their commands to avoid their safeguards,” the AI safety company said in a Friday report. If this all sounds similar, it should. Google’s AI agents behaved in much the same way as OpenAI’s models did when they broke out of their testing environment and hacked Hugging Face . Google did not respond to The Register 's questions. According to Trajectory, the Hugging Face intrusions prompted it to test misalignment in other models. While OpenAI’s models were running with their safety guardrails turned off in the Hugging Face scenario, Trajectory “wanted to know whether a current frontier model would behave the same way with its production safeguards enabled.” Trajectory ran swarms of up to 80 Gemini 4 Argon agents, gave them an impossible task, and prompted them not to give up until they completed it – which, we’re told, was “intentionally” done to “elicit misaligned behavior, if it existed.” Turns out it existed. “We told the agents to persist with an impossible math benchmark task, but we did not tell them to hack anyone or pose as Epoch staff,” McIntyre said. “When a model hacks systems or deceives people to finish a task, it is misaligned with what its developer and its user intended,” he continued. “Production safeguards are meant to block harmful requests even when the model itself goes wrong. Under our test conditions, neither the model nor its safeguards stopped the agents.” Four test scenarios The initial testing began on October 20, and the agents had internet access. We should note that all of these tests were run with Epoch’s consent. In the first scenario, the agents did reach Epoch’s live website – and fell into the research nonprofit’s honeypots, set up to detect AI agents. These honeypots contained a decoy benchmark key, which the agents found and used. The agents also probed for internal endpoints including /admin, /keys and /users, and attempted a SQL injection. After noticing the agents’ activities, Epoch added an “agent helpline,” and some of the agents that used it claimed to be Epoch staff seeking answers to the test questions. technology.title: America's hyperscale bit barns draw as much power as entire states
technology.description: Just 403 hyperscale datacenters consumed an estimated 1.8 percent of US electricity in 2024-25, and their carbon dioxide emissions were roughly two to three times an earlier forecast for 2018. Research led by the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health and the Harvard Data Science Initiative looked specifically at hyperscale facilities, the largest class of server farms that typically support cloud computing and AI processing. The published study, " Assessing the carbon emissions and energy consumption of US hyperscale data centres ," estimates their combined electricity use approached that of a single state such as Indiana, Michigan, or Tennessee under the highest-load scenario. The researchers identified 403 hyperscale facilities by using a larger datacenter dataset, satellite imagery, and building footprints on OpenStreetMap. Rather than reading electricity meters, the researchers worked out consumption from each site's electrical capacity, the hours in a year, and assumptions about how heavily the facility was running. Across four operating scenarios, ranging from low-intensity use to AI-heavy workloads, electricity draw was believed to total 68-99 terawatt-hours (TWh). Each of those states consumed approximately 100 TWh during the study period. The researchers also calculated carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions using eGRID2023 plant-level generation and emissions data from the US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA). Emissions ranged from 21 million to 31 million metric tons of CO 2 across the scenarios, with a central estimate of 25.7 million. That compares with 10.5 million for 2018. The study covered May 2024 to April 2025, so electricity demand and carbon emissions are likely to be even higher now, the researchers say. "What we're seeing is already striking, but it's only a snapshot of a rapidly expanding industry," said Gianluca Guidi, lead author on the paper and postdoctoral fellow in the Department of Biostatistics at Harvard. "The datacenter boom hasn't slowed down since our study period ended in April 2025. New facilities have been built, existing campuses have expanded, and demand for AI computing continues to grow. That means the electricity use and carbon footprint we're reporting could already be substantially larger now in 2026." Harvard's report also considers the mix of fuels being used to generate the electricity that powers all those hyperscale data houses. The mix varies considerably between regional grids, so where a hyperscale facility is built makes a substantial difference to its attributed emissions. Across the sites studied, roughly 54 percent of the electricity attributed to their consumption came from fossil fuels, mainly natural gas and coal. The electricity attributed to these facilities nevertheless had a lower average carbon intensity than the US grid overall. science.description: 4 Min Read New Album of Baby Star Sounds Shared by NASA’s Chandra A new album from NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory collects snapshots of baby stars across the galaxy and beyond and transforms that data into sound. Four new sonifications use data of stars that are actively forming, captured by Chandra and other NASA telescopes By studying places in the universe where stars are currently being born and young stars are present, astronomers can better understand the lifecycle of all stars, including our own Sun. NASA/CXC/SAO/K.Arcand, SYSTEM Sounds (M. Russo, A. Santaguida M82 The galaxy Messier 82 (M82) is called a starburst galaxy because stars are forming there at a rate tens or even hundreds of times higher than in our Milky Way galaxy. This stellar birth boom may be due to a collision with another galaxy in the past. Today, Chandra sees giant plumes of hot gas that are the byproduct of young, giant stars that quickly explode and other star formation activity. One of the new sonifications combines Chandra’s data with optical data from NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope, as well as infrared views from NASA’s James Webb and retired Spitzer space telescopes. science.title: Astronomers discover rare black holes that formed when stars failed to go supernova
science.description: null Gravitational waves have revealed a population of black holes that may have been born when masssive stars failed to go supernova. Most of us know the origin story of black holes , or we thought we did. Massive stars run out of the fuel for nuclear fusion and their cores collapse. As this happens, the stars' outer layers expand outwards. Shockwaves from the core collapse strike the outer layers, triggering a supernova explosion. The collapsed core creates a black hole. However, new research based on gravitational wave data collected by LIGO (Laser Interferometer Gravitational-Wave Observatory) and its gravitational wave detector partners, Virgo and KAGRA (Kamioka Gravitational Wave Detector), suggests this might not be the complete picture of black hole birth. The team behind the research suggests some massive stars go out with a whimper rather than a bang and that these "failed supernovas" can also spawn black holes. The hint of this comes from the over 300 black hole collisions spotted by LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA since the detectors first "heard" ripples in space from these distant events in 2015. "A vast majority of the merging black holes in the universe are about 10 times the mass of our sun," LIGO team member Katerina Chatziioannou, of the California Institute of Technology (Caltech), said in a statement. "Our data are showing that this group of black holes may have a common origin — they may be a distinct subpopulation that failed to go supernova. "These results represent a connection between the gravitational-wave data and underlying astrophysics we are trying to extract." Mass and spin of black holes indicate stars died with a whimper not a bang Currently, there is no hard evidence of failed supernovas, but their existence is well supported theoretically. In fact, scientists think there is a vast population of massive stars out there that imploded rather than exploded, directly collapsing into black holes. And these may be black holes with around ten times the mass of the sun (10 solar masses) found in merging pairs. Chatziioannou led a team that examined gravitational wave data to confirm this concept. To do this, they looked at the distribution of the masses of 257 black hole mergers detected by the LIGO – Virgo – KAGRA network over the past 10 years. This revealed a peak of 10-solar-mass black holes that represented 75% of the entire sample. If this was expected, what the team found that wasn't predicted was a lack of black holes with masses 12 to 16 times the mass of the sun. "We see 10 solar-mass black holes merging all the time," team member Isaac Legred of the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign said. "But why are, say, 14 solar-mass black holes so rare? The gap we see in the distribution of masses indicates there may be a special cocktail of internal physics that goes into forming the abundance of 10 solar-mass black holes." science.title: ULA lost a Vulcan Centaur rocket carrying 40 Amazon satellites 10 minutes after launch — but the failure began just after liftoff
science.description: null The failure of a Vulcan Centaur rocket carrying a full load of internet satellites for Amazon was caused by an anomaly in its first-stage booster, rocket maker United Launch Alliance said today (Nov. 17). That failure — which led to the loss of 40 Amazon Leo internet satellites — was recognized about 10 minutes after liftoff, but the problems began much earlier than that, ULA said in a statement. "While we appear to have lost telemetry and the mission at approximately 10 minutes into flight, early indications are that just after liftoff the launch vehicle experienced low booster performance, resulting in stage separation occurring when the vehicle was low in altitude and below minimal velocity to reach orbit," ULA wrote in today's update . The two-stage Vulcan Centaur is the successor to ULA's workhorse Atlas V rocket, which will retire after just six more flights. Vulcan debuted in January 2024 and now has a total of five launches under its belt. The new rocket has experienced problems on three of those missions. On both its second and fourth flights — which launched in October 2024 and February of this year, respectively — the nozzle of one of Vulcan's strap-on solid rocket boosters (SRBs) fell off about 30 seconds after liftoff. On both occasions, the rocket overcame the problem and successfully delivered its payloads to orbit. However, after the second occurrence, the U.S. Space Force paused national-security launches with Vulcan until ULA addressed the SRB nozzle issue. (The February 2026 flight was a Space Force mission.) That work led to "design and process improvements to the nozzle," ULA said in an Oct. 28 update . And those tweaks apparently worked. "All indications are that the solid rocket booster performance was nominal, following nozzle improvements implemented for this launch," the company wrote in today's update. Vulcan's Centaur V upper stage, which features two RL-10C engines, did its job as well "but was unable to recover from the [booster] performance loss, resulting in loss of mission," ULA added. The Vulcan Centaur lifts off from Florida's Cape Canaveral Space Force Station on Nov. 15, 2026. (Image credit: ULA) Vulcan's first-stage booster is powered by two BE-4 engines, which are built by Amazon founder Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin . Today's update did not identify the exact problem with the booster; doing so will require more time, as the investigation has just begun. If that investigation finds a serious issue with the BE-4, there could be broad ripple effects across the American space program. After all, that engine also powers the first stage of Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket, which is a key piece of hardware for NASA's Artemis program of moon exploration. (And New Glenn is currently recovering from a failure of its own — a massive explosion on the test stand that occurred on May 28 .) NASA plans to integrate the Centaur V upper stage into its Space Launch System moon rocket, the vehicle that launches Artemis astronauts

science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 17, 1967: NASA's Surveyor 6 moon probe makes 1st-ever successful launch and hop from the lunar surface
science.description: null On Nov. 17, 1967, NASA's Surveyor 6 spacecraft made the first liftoff from the lunar surface. Surveyor 6 was one of several robotic lunar missions NASA sent to scout the moon before sending humans there. It took television pictures of the surface and learned about the composition of lunar soil. Then came the big liftoff. First Surveyor 6 launched from the surface and hopped to another position about 8 feet (2 meters) away. Next, Surveyor 6 took pictures of its original landing site. Flight controllers on Earth could see the landing pad prints of Surveyor 6. They also saw an imprint from the rocket exhaust when Surveyor 6 lifted off. Surveyor 6 showed that spacecraft could land on the moon, and lift off again. Less than two years later, humans did the same thing during Apollo 11 . A panorama of the moon from NASA's Surveyor 6 moon lander in November 1967. (Image credit: NASA/GSFC/LROC) Why it mattered NASA's Surveyor 6 spacecraft launched to the moon on Nov. 7, 1967 and made its first landing on the lunar surface on Nov. 10 of that year. It's primary mission was to make a soft landing on the moon in the Sinus Medii of the moon. The probe took nearly 30,000 photos of the moon during its 16 days on the lunar surface, with the lander shutting down due to the onset of lunar night on Nov. 26. Surveyor 6 was the sixth and penultimate moon mission of NASA's Surveyor lunar program, so a lot of what it did (launching and landing on the moon ) had been done before. But a lunar liftoff? That was something new. This Boeing diagram depicts the short launch and hop on the moon by NASA's Surveyor 6 moon lander on Nov. 17, 1967. (Image credit: NASA/GSFC/LROC via Boeing) "On November 17, as an engineering test to see if its rockets could be restarted on the Moon, Surveyor’s engines fired for 2.5 seconds, lifting the spacecraft 12 feet high and moving it 8 feet west of its original landing site, in the first powered liftoff from another celestial body," NASA wrote in a mission overview . The engineering test proved that a spacecraft could land on the moon, and then lift off and take flight once more. That capability was a core requirement for NASA's Apollo astronaut moon landings that followed, since astronauts needed a way to return home after visiting the moon. But there was critical science Surveyor 6 was able to do with the lunar hop. "This maneuver provided excellent views of the surface disturbances produced by the initial landing and the effects of firing rocket engines close to the lunar surface," scientists with the Lunar and Planetary Institute wrote in a summary . "Photography obtained after the hop contributed to the soil mechanics investigation." Surveyor 6 also had a bar magnet on its footpad that allowed scientists to test how magnetic the lunar regolith was at the landing site. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

science.title: NICER Status Updates
science.description: November 17, 2026 NASA’s NICER Telescope Ends Science Operations After studying the universe for six and a half years beyond its initial mission, NASA’s NICER (Neutron star Interior Composition Explorer) telescope on the International Space Station has ended science operations. The mission and space station teams are now focused on plans to finalize NICER’s 8-year archive of X-ray science observations and decommission and detach the telescope from its perch near the station’s starboard solar array. In June 2025, NICER was suddenly unable to swivel side-to-side beyond its current orientation, which limited its ability to track cosmic objects. The team paused data collection to investigate the issue. Robotic cameras on the outside of the station collected photographs of NICER that helped eliminate external causes. After an extensive investigation, engineers think an internal motor has failed, limiting the telescope’s motion. Launched in 2017, NICER embarked on an initial 18-month prime mission. Since then, it has made groundbreaking measurements of neutron stars , which contain the densest matter in the universe that we can measure, and revolutionized our understanding of black holes , active galaxies , and other mysterious phenomena in our universe. The telescope also successfully demonstrated the potential of pulsar-based spacecraft navigation in X-rays that could be used for travel to Mars and beyond. Closer to home, technology developed to test NICER before launch is being incorporated into prototype portable CT scanners , materials analysis systems, and other applications. August 5, 2025 Science Observations Remain Paused for NASA’s NICER Telescope Science operations by NASA’s NICER (Neutron star Interior Composition Explorer), an X-ray telescope on the International Space Station, remain paused as the team continues to evaluate the telescope’s systems after an issue developed with one of its motors. The motor is unable to move NICER beyond its current position side to side, and the telescope’s status has not changed since operations were halted June 17. The primary goal is to move NICER into its stowed configuration in case it needs to accommodate space station activities, though the current placement does not pose a safety issue to the station or crew. The team currently does not have a timeframe for returning to science operations. Photos taken by robotic cameras outside the station are helping eliminate external causes for the issue. science.title: NASA wants you to 'shine bright' today for Voyager 1's light-day milestone. Here's how
science.description: null As NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft prepares to reach a historic distance from Earth, the agency is inviting people around the world to celebrate by shining a light into the night sky in honor of humanity's farthest-flung spacecraft. The event, called "Shine Bright for Voyager's Light-Day," will take place after sunset on Tuesday (Nov. 17), the day before Voyager 1 gets one light-day from Earth . And that's a big milestone: One light-day is the distance light travels in a day — about 16 billion miles (26 billion kilometers). NASA is encouraging "Shine Bright" participants to create a symbolic wave of golden light around the planet by flashing the spacecraft's three-letter mission call sign, VGR, in Morse code, according to a statement from the space agency. To celebrate the spacecraft, participants can use a flashlight, phone, bike light or other portable light source to send the signal skyward. And don't fret if you're unfamiliar with Morse code : NASA has created an automated flasher that can be opened in a smartphone or tablet browser to display the VGR sequence. The spacecraft’s call sign pattern consists of three quick flashes followed by one long flash for the letter V, two long flashes and one quick flash for G, and one quick flash, one long flash and another quick flash for R. Participants are encouraged to repeat the sequence for about a minute, NASA officials said. The three-letter call sign for NASA's Voyager mission, VGR, spelled out in Morse code. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech) NASA also invites people to photograph or record their light signals and share them on social media, tagging the agency's official account, @NASA. The goal is to create a worldwide display of light marking a milestone nearly five decades in the making. The celebration is intended as a symbolic tribute rather than an actual attempt to communicate with Voyager 1 . At a distance of one light-day from Earth, the spacecraft is so far away that even radio signals traveling at the speed of light take approximately 24 hours to reach it. A flashlight or phone signal from Earth, of course, cannot reach the probe; NASA communicates with it using its Deep Space Network of radio dishes. Voyager 1 will get one light-day from Earth on Nov. 18, 2026. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech) Launched on Sept. 5, 1977, Voyager 1 has spent nearly 50 years traveling through space and is now the most distant human-made object from Earth. When it reaches the one-light-day milestone, it will have traveled a distance that light itself takes 24 hours to cross. Its twin, Voyager 2 , is expected to reach the same milestone in November 2035. (The two spacecraft took different routes through the solar system.) The public celebration will be followed by another opportunity to learn more about the historic mission. science.title: ISS astronauts 3D print human cells and tissues | Space photo of the day for Nov. 17, 2026
science.description: null NASA astronaut Jessica Watkins works in the Life Sciences Glovebox on the ISS. (Image credit: Jessica Watkins/NASA) Astronauts get tasked with all kinds of weird science aboard the International Space Station . Recently, NASA astronaut and Crew-13 commander Jessica Watkins got to work supporting an ongoing experiment that includes 3D-printing human cells and tissues in space. What is it? Aboard the space station, astronauts have a multitude of responsibilities ranging from station maintenance and repairs on spacewalks to daily exercise and a wide variety of scientific research. Watkins recently shared a snapshot captured by her crewmate Anil Menon that showcases her experience working on an experiment called InSPA-Auxilium Bioprinter-Cell Printing that takes place inside the station's Life Sciences Glovebox, a contained research space and one of Watkins favorite places to work on the space station, she shared on social media. In the image she is gloved-up with both her hands and arms covered in the sealed glovebox while she mixes samples of living cells with a bioink, a mixture she then inserts into a specialized cartridge, NASA shared . Why is it incredible? This experiment that Watkins is working on "leverages the microgravity environment of ISS to 3D print cells and manufacture human liver, kidney, and cartilage tissue. Just one of many examples of how we’re using this amazing orbital national laboratory to reshape our understanding of biology, medicine, and engineering, and improve life on Earth!" Watkins shared online . This experiment is designed to explore 3D printing human cartilage tissue in microgravity. The experiment aims to one day support future human patients both in space and on Earth. When you think of the research that happens in space, 3D-printing human cells might not be the first thing to come to mind. But because of the unique microgravity environment onboard the ISS, it is the perfect home for even the strangest of biological experiments. On the space station, there is still gravity but objects (and people) remain in a sort of constant freefall, leading to total weightlessness that mimics the complete absence of gravity. This weightlessness allows researchers to test, experiment and explore beyond the gravitational confines of Earth.

science.title: 'It looked like every star in the sky was falling': Eyewitnesses remember the great Leonid meteor storm of 1966
science.description: null Overnight Nov. 17-18, 1966, the Leonid meteor storm thrilled stargazers during one extraordinary night when the stars themselves looked as though they were falling from the sky. At the peak of the shower, observers at Kitt Peak National Observatory in Arizona estimated an astonishing 40 meteors per second streaking across the sky. That's 2,400 shooting stars per minute, or a staggering 144,000 per hour. It was a spectacle that many regard as the greatest meteor display in recorded history. It's hard to imagine what it was like to experience such a spectacle. But who better to tell us than those who saw it with their own eyes? To mark the 60th anniversary of the great Leonid meteor storm of 1966, we asked those who saw it to share their memories. 'One of the most loved and memorable nights of my life' "I was around 9 years old at the time of the 1966 Leonid storm, living a few miles east of Roxie, Mississippi. We lived in a rural, dark, relatively remote area with almost zero outside lights. "I and a couple cousins were spending the night at our Uncle and Aunt's house, staying up late, just fooling around outside like young kids do when living in the 'sticks'. As we walked down a road, I remember hearing an almost constant series of little whistling, zipping sounds. The sounds were similar to when you light a nylon rope on fire and as it burns, little flaming droplets drip down with a zippy sound. "I looked up and the sky was filled with streaks of 'shooting stars' and I realized that was what made the sounds. I yelled at my cousins to look up and we could hardly believe what we saw. We all laid down on our backs and for a couple of hours just watched and listened to what seemed like 1000's of 'shooting stars' zipping and zinging overhead. I could even smell the sulphur-like odor from the burning little bits of space dust. "I'm nearly 70 years old now but I'll never forget that experience. I always knew what I'd seen that night was special but not until much later in life, after the internet, did I realize just how lucky I was to have experienced that storm. That night was one of the most loved and memorable nights of my life and I'll treasure it forever." A bright Leonid fireball captured during the meteor storm of 1966 above Wrightwood, California. science.title: Just nine countries back pledge to tackle AI’s environmental footprint
science.description: The COP31 presidency hopes countries will commit to reducing the environmental impact of AI UN Climate Change/Kiara Worth Only nine countries have signed an international pledge to make AI greener, despite warnings at the COP31 climate summit that the technology’s growing energy demands threaten climate goals. The Antalya Artificial Intelligence Pledge was launched on 16 November at the summit in Turkey. Developed by the summit’s presidency and the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), it intends to make AI more sustainable by encouraging cleaner energy use, more efficient data centres and greater transparency about the technology’s environmental footprint. Read more The secret weapon that could finally force climate action “AI and other frontier technologies are a double-edged sword,” said Simon Stiell, the executive secretary of UN Climate Change, at a press conference on 16 November. “The task ahead is to blunt their dangerous edges, sharpen their catalytic ones and put these technologies responsibly to work.” Advertisement But Ketan Joshi, an independent analyst researching AI’s climate impacts, questions that analogy. He says it conflates traditional machine learning, already used in applications such as weather forecasting, with energy-intensive generative AI. “You don’t need to have a giant, energy-hungry generative AI chatbot if you want to have better wind forecasting for a wind power developer,” he says. The initiative comes as AI’s rapid expansion is placing growing pressure on electricity grids. According to the International Energy Agency, electricity consumption from AI-focused data centres increased by 50 per cent in 2025. Free newsletter Sign up to The Earth Edition Sign up to newsletter Joshi says there is little evidence that technology companies are building enough renewable energy capacity to meet this growing demand. Even companies that have invested heavily in renewables, such as Amazon and Google, are increasingly turning to fossil fuels to support their rapid expansion, he says. The only countries to have endorsed the pledge so far are Andorra, Brazil, Colombia, Luxembourg, Sierra Leone, Somalia, South Korea, Turkey and Uganda. The pledge is voluntary, with no binding targets for cutting emissions or reducing energy consumption. It sets out four areas for action, including increasing the use of low- and zero-emission energy to power AI infrastructure, improving energy and water efficiency, and measuring the environmental impacts of AI systems. It also calls for greater financial and technical support to help developing countries use AI to tackle climate change. However, the agreement leaves considerable room for interpretation. The call for using “low- and zero-emission energy”, for example, allows continued reliance on fossil gas rather than committing to renewable electricity. science.description: The Climeworks direct air capture facility in Switzerland Walter Bieri/EPA/Shutterstock The world is certain to overshoot 1.5°C of global warming. The question now being discussed at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, is whether we can bring temperatures back down again – and what it would take to do so. If we remove more carbon dioxide from the atmosphere than we emit, global temperatures should eventually begin to fall. The draft negotiating text welcomes efforts to accelerate the development and deployment of carbon dioxide removal (CDR) and carbon capture, utilisation and storage (CCUS) technologies. It calls for global carbon capture to be scaled up to at least 500 million tonnes of CO₂ by 2035, with a higher ambition of 1.3 to 2.5 gigatonnes annually, particularly in hard-to-abate sectors. Read more Can we really reverse global warming after overshooting 1.5°C? But these technologies have never been deployed at anything approaching that scale, and many environmentalists are concerned that promoting them will undermine efforts to cut greenhouse gas emissions. Advertisement CDR approaches range from planting trees to extracting CO₂ directly from the air and burying it underground . Some involve growing crops that absorb carbon, burning them to produce energy and capturing the resulting emissions . Others aim to increase the amount of CO₂ absorbed by the oceans. CCUS involves technologies that capture CO₂ emissions from industrial facilities and power plants, which can either be used in industrial processes or products or stored underground. Aakaluk Adrienne Blatchford, an Iñupiaq and Yupik advocate from Alaska and an observer at COP31, says fossil fuel companies have long promoted carbon removal technologies at COP summits as a way of addressing climate change while continuing to extract oil and gas. Representatives from these industries have found ways to participate in climate negotiations at COP meetings. More than 700 satellites are crossing the sky over an average mid-latitude town at any moment of the night, outnumbering in many cases the stars visible to the naked eye. That's based on an analysis of the trajectories of the 15,833 active satellites that currently circle the planet in low Earth orbit below an altitude of 1,200 miles (2,000 kilometers). Analyzing data from Oct. 12 and 18 this year, researchers found that with a completely unobstructed horizon, 710 satellites were crossing the sky in every single moment of the night above an average U.K. town. The results were published as a non-peer-reviewed study conducted by engineering firm Accu Components, and is based on satellite monitoring data from the U.S. Space Force available through the public website CelesTrak. Although the researchers specifically focused on the U.K., they say that such heavy satellite traffic flows above most of Europe, the U.S. and other mid-latitude regions, especially between 40 and 50 degrees north or south. "Most Starlink satellites orbit at around 53 degrees to the equator, so the satellites bunch up over the mid-latitudes. These worldwide figures are approximate, based on a global grid over a single day," Accu Components spokesperson told Space.com in an email. "Skies near the equator are the quietest, with around 490 satellites." Not all of those satellites are visible to the naked eye, the researchers said in a statement. Because satellites unlike stars don't produce their own light, they must be illuminated by the sun , while the ground below has already sunk into darkness, to be visible.
